title: Bayesian network model improves risk stratification in pulmonary arterial hypertension
summary: A tree-augmented naive Bayes model called PHORA was derived on the REVEAL registry, using the REVEAL 2.0 variables, to predict 1-year survival in pulmonary arterial hypertension. It reached an AUC of 0.80 versus 0.76 for REVEAL 2.0, and AUCs of 0.74 and 0.80 in the external COMPERA and PHSANZ registries. The improvement over the existing tool is modest and the data are retrospective registries.
ai_technology: PHORA, a tree-augmented naive Bayes network

evidence.tested: Internal validation in REVEAL and external validation in the COMPERA and PHSANZ registries.
evidence.unknown: Prospective benefit over REVEAL 2.0 in practice; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Models dependencies between prognostic variables to predict 1-year survival.
